text: Think outside the box.
pedagogical_cue: 'Think' is voiceless /θ/ — air only. 'the' is voiced /ð/ — same tongue, add a buzz.

text: Through thick and thin.
pedagogical_cue: Three /θ/ starts in a row: reset the tongue tip to your teeth before each one.

text: Worth the extra effort.
pedagogical_cue: Round the lips for /w/, finish 'worth' with air at the teeth, then glide into a voiced 'the'.

text: Healthy teeth and gums.
pedagogical_cue: Don't let the final /θ/ in 'teeth' turn into /t/ or /s/ before 'and'.

text: I thought about thirty-three things this morning.
pedagogical_cue: Four voiceless /θ/ starts, then a voiced /ð/ in 'this' — keep each one airy as you speed up.

text: The author chose a thoughtful theme.
pedagogical_cue: 'The' is voiced /ð/, 'author', 'thoughtful' and 'theme' are voiceless /θ/ — same tongue, different buzz.

text: Her healthy tooth was throbbing throughout the night.
pedagogical_cue: Watch the final /θ/ in 'tooth' before the /w/ of 'was'.

text: We need a thorough method for growth.
pedagogical_cue: Keep the /θ/ in 'method' and the final /θ/ in 'growth' — they are easy to drop at speed.

text: Three tall trees grew along the track.
pedagogical_cue: three = friction you can stretch; tall, trees, track = a quick stop.

text: Thanks for your help on Thursday.
pedagogical_cue: Start 'thanks' and 'Thursday' with the tongue tip lightly between the teeth and a soft push of air — no /t/ tap.

text: Happy birthday, have a wonderful month!
pedagogical_cue: The /θ/ sits in the middle of 'birthday' and at the end of 'month': keep the air flowing at the teeth.

text: Both of us think it's worth it.
pedagogical_cue: Three voiceless /θ/ sounds: finish 'both' and 'worth' with air at the teeth, not a /t/ or /s/.

text: Nothing is healthier than a good night's sleep.
pedagogical_cue: Keep 'nothing' airy at the teeth, and don't swap the /θ/ in 'healthier' for an /f/.

text: My math teacher is very thorough.
pedagogical_cue: 'Math' ends in /θ/, not /s/; 'thorough' starts with it — tongue out, gentle air.

text: Breathe in fresh air.
pedagogical_cue: 'Breathe' ends in voiced /ð/ — feel the buzz on your tongue as you link into 'in'.

text: Smooth as leather.
pedagogical_cue: Two voiced /ð/ sounds: keep the tongue light at the teeth, never a hard /d/.

text: They walked together through the chilly autumn weather.
pedagogical_cue: Voiced /ð/ in 'they', 'together', 'the', 'weather'; voiceless /θ/ only in 'through'.

text: It was worthwhile, although they were tired.
pedagogical_cue: 'Although' and 'they' are voiced /ð/; 'worthwhile' hides a voiceless /θ/ right before a /w/.

text: They dare to go there together.
pedagogical_cue: they = soft buzz at the teeth; dare = a quick tap behind the teeth.

text: Let's get together this weekend.
pedagogical_cue: Voiced /ð/ in 'together' and 'this': tongue tip at the teeth, voice on, feel the buzz.

text: The weather is lovely today.
pedagogical_cue: Keep the /ð/ in the middle of 'weather' soft and buzzing — not a hard /d/.

text: My mother and father live there.
pedagogical_cue: Three voiced /ð/ sounds: let the tongue rest lightly on the teeth and keep your voice going.

text: I'd rather stay with my brother.
pedagogical_cue: In 'rather' and 'brother' the /ð/ links two vowels — keep it smooth, never a /d/ or /z/.

text: Those clothes are smoother than these.
pedagogical_cue: Lots of voiced /ð/: keep the buzz at your teeth and don't let it slide into /z/.

text: Breathe slowly and soothe your mind.
pedagogical_cue: 'Breathe' and 'soothe' end in a long voiced /ð/ — hold the buzz before the next word.

text: Is it this one or that one?
pedagogical_cue: Start 'this' and 'that' with a light voiced buzz at the teeth, not a /d/.

text: Either way, they will be there.
pedagogical_cue: 'Either', 'they' and 'there': tongue tip touches the teeth, voice on, then glide away.

text: We did it without them.
pedagogical_cue: 'Without' and 'them' use a soft voiced /ð/; compare it with the hard /d/ of 'did'.

text: I think the kitchen sink is clean.
pedagogical_cue: think = tongue at the teeth; sink = tongue behind the teeth.

text: Take a deep breath and pass the test.
pedagogical_cue: breath ends with air between the teeth; pass and test end with a sharp hiss behind them.

text: The thick soup made me sick.
pedagogical_cue: thick = tongue between the teeth; sick and soup = tongue behind them with a sharp hiss.

text: Think of a song to sing.
pedagogical_cue: think = air through the teeth; song and sing = a hiss from behind them.

text: Walk the path and pass the gate.
pedagogical_cue: path ends with soft air at the teeth; pass ends with a hiss behind them.

text: Her faith shows on her face.
pedagogical_cue: faith ends at the teeth; face ends with an /s/ hiss behind them.

text: Three seats are still free.
pedagogical_cue: three = tongue out, soft air; seats and still = tongue back, sharp hiss.

text: Math class starts at seven.
pedagogical_cue: math = soft friction at the teeth; class, starts and seven = tongue behind the teeth.

text: Thank you, Sam, for the seat.
pedagogical_cue: thank = tongue between the teeth; Sam and seat = tongue tucked behind them.

text: Both sides agree on this.
pedagogical_cue: both ends with air at the teeth; sides starts with a hiss behind them.

text: My tooth hurts when I sip tea.
pedagogical_cue: tooth = air between the teeth; sip and hurts = a sharp /s/ behind them.

text: Is it thin or simply small?
pedagogical_cue: thin = tongue out and soft; simply and small = tongue in and hissing.

text: Thursday is the first sunny day.
pedagogical_cue: Thursday = tongue at the teeth; sunny and first = a clean /s/ hiss.

text: We went to view the very wide valley.
pedagogical_cue: /w/ = rounded lips, no teeth. /v/ = top teeth touch the lower lip.

text: The wide valley has a lovely view.
pedagogical_cue: wide = rounded lips, no teeth; valley and view = top teeth on the lower lip.

text: It's very warm this evening.
pedagogical_cue: warm = lips rounded like 'oo'; very and evening = teeth touch the lip and buzz.

text: We visited a village by the river.
pedagogical_cue: we = rounded lips; visited, village and river = teeth on the lower lip.

text: The wind moved the vines.
pedagogical_cue: wind = round your lips; vines and moved = teeth gently on the lower lip.

text: Would you like a vanilla waffle?
pedagogical_cue: would and waffle = rounded lips; vanilla = teeth on the lip with a buzz.

text: Her voice was warm and lovely.
pedagogical_cue: warm and was = rounded lips; voice and lovely = teeth on the lower lip.

text: We have five weeks of vacation.
pedagogical_cue: we and weeks = rounded lips; five, have and vacation = teeth touch the lip.

text: Wear a vest when it's windy.
pedagogical_cue: wear, when and windy = lips round, teeth away; vest = teeth on the lip.

text: Every Wednesday we watch a movie.
pedagogical_cue: Wednesday, we and watch = rounded lips; every and movie = teeth on the lower lip.

text: I'll wait for the next van.
pedagogical_cue: wait = start with rounded lips; van = start with teeth on the lower lip.

text: We value what we have.
pedagogical_cue: we and what = rounded lips; value and have = teeth on the lip, voice on.

text: Her business is doing really well.
pedagogical_cue: In 'business' the first s is a buzzing /z/ and the last a hissing /s/ — feel the switch in your throat.

text: The old houses rise above the streets.
pedagogical_cue: 'Houses' and 'rise' buzz with /z/; 'streets' hisses with /s/ — hand on your throat to feel it.

text: A cool breeze rises from the sea.
pedagogical_cue: Hold the buzz to the very end of 'breeze' and 'rises'; 'sea' is pure air.

text: She always says yes to new ideas.
pedagogical_cue: 'Says' starts with /s/ and ends with /z/; 'yes' ends with a clean /s/ hiss.

text: Prices rise as the season changes.
pedagogical_cue: Keep the voice on for the endings of 'prices' and 'changes' — /ɪz/, not /ɪs/.

text: He loses his keys twice a week.
pedagogical_cue: 'Loses', 'his' and 'keys' end in voiced /z/; 'twice' ends with a sharp /s/.

text: These sauces taste amazing.
pedagogical_cue: 'Sauces' starts with /s/ and ends with /ɪz/; keep 'amazing' buzzy in the middle.

text: The bus was full of tourists.
pedagogical_cue: 'Bus' ends with a hiss; 'was' ends with a buzz — don't devoice it to 'wass'.

text: Close the door and choose a seat.
pedagogical_cue: The verb 'close' and 'choose' end in buzzing /z/; 'seat' starts with a hiss.

text: My nieces visit us on Sundays.
pedagogical_cue: 'Visit' and 'Sundays' carry a voiced /z/; 'us' ends with an unvoiced /s/.

text: She sells roses at the market.
pedagogical_cue: 'Sells' starts with /s/ and ends with /z/; both s letters in 'roses' buzz.

text: Use this rice for the dishes.
pedagogical_cue: The verb 'use' ends with a buzz, 'rice' with a hiss, and 'dishes' with /ɪz/.

text: I feel you should fill the form.
pedagogical_cue: 'Feel' = long, smiling /iː/; 'fill' = short, relaxed /ɪ/ with a looser jaw.

text: Please leave if you live nearby.
pedagogical_cue: Stretch 'leave' and 'please'; keep 'live' short and lax.

text: Each scene in this film works.
pedagogical_cue: Long tense /iː/ in 'each' and 'scene'; short lax /ɪ/ in 'this' and 'film'.

text: We need to sleep a little.
pedagogical_cue: Hold 'need' and 'sleep' longer with spread lips; 'little' is quick and relaxed.

text: Keep the ship clean and quick.
pedagogical_cue: 'Keep' and 'clean' are long and tense; 'ship' and 'quick' are short — not 'sheep'.

text: Please sit in your seat.
pedagogical_cue: 'Seat' is long with smiling lips; 'sit' is short with a relaxed tongue.

text: The team will win this week.
pedagogical_cue: Long /iː/ in 'team' and 'week'; short /ɪ/ in 'will' and 'win'.

text: Eat a bit of cheese.
pedagogical_cue: Stretch 'eat' and 'cheese'; cut 'bit' short so it doesn't become 'beat'.

text: She bought cheap chips today.
pedagogical_cue: 'Cheap' = long /iː/; 'chips' = short /ɪ/ — the vowel length carries the meaning.

text: Read the list and keep it.
pedagogical_cue: Long in 'read' and 'keep'; short and relaxed in 'list' and 'it'.

text: Meet me at six, please.
pedagogical_cue: Smile and hold 'meet' and 'please'; 'six' is short with a looser jaw.

text: The heat makes it hard to think.
pedagogical_cue: 'Heat' is long and tense; 'it' and 'think' use the short lax /ɪ/.

text: Let's change the project action plan.
pedagogical_cue: Round your lips slightly for /tʃ/, /dʒ/ and /ʃ/; 'change' starts with /tʃ/ and ends with /dʒ/.

text: Check the bridge before the big shift.
pedagogical_cue: 'Check' = stop + hiss /tʃ/; 'bridge' ends in voiced /dʒ/; 'shift' = smooth /ʃ/ with no stop.

text: Each manager shares a short report.
pedagogical_cue: Lips pushed forward: /tʃ/ in 'each', /dʒ/ in 'manager', /ʃ/ in 'shares' and 'short'.

text: Join the chat and share your ideas.
pedagogical_cue: 'Join' = voiced /dʒ/, 'chat' = unvoiced /tʃ/, 'share' = /ʃ/ with no stop at the start.

text: She just changed the schedule.
pedagogical_cue: Keep /ʃ/ in 'she' soft and rounded; 'just' and 'schedule' carry a voiced /dʒ/.

text: Choose a large dish for lunch.
pedagogical_cue: 'Choose' and 'lunch' have /tʃ/; 'large' ends with /dʒ/; 'dish' ends with a long /ʃ/.

text: The coach shared a generous suggestion.
pedagogical_cue: 'Coach' ends with /tʃ/, 'shared' starts with /ʃ/, 'generous' starts with voiced /dʒ/.

text: Watch the jet engine in action.
pedagogical_cue: 'Watch' ends in /tʃ/, 'jet' and 'engine' use /dʒ/, and 'action' hides a /ʃ/.

text: This situation needs a major change.
pedagogical_cue: 'Situation' has /tʃ/ then /ʃ/; 'major' has /dʒ/ — keep the lips slightly rounded.

text: Teachers judge each special project fairly.
pedagogical_cue: /tʃ/ in 'teachers' and 'each', /dʒ/ in 'judge' and 'project', /ʃ/ in 'special'.

text: I enjoy fresh cheese and juice.
pedagogical_cue: 'Enjoy' and 'juice' start with voiced /dʒ/; 'cheese' with /tʃ/; 'fresh' ends in /ʃ/.

text: Should we charge the budget now?
pedagogical_cue: 'Should' = soft /ʃ/; 'charge' = /tʃ/ … /dʒ/; 'budget' = voiced /dʒ/ in the middle.

text: The results are really clear.
pedagogical_cue: For /r/ pull the tongue back without touching anything; for /l/ press the tip behind the top teeth.

text: The world is a large place.
pedagogical_cue: No rolled r in 'large': pull the tongue back; let the /l/ in 'world' and 'place' touch the ridge.

text: Please read the list aloud.
pedagogical_cue: 'Read' = lips slightly round, tongue touching nothing; 'list' = tongue tip touching the ridge.

text: Light rain fell all morning.
pedagogical_cue: 'Rain' = tongue pulled back, lips slightly round; 'light' and 'fell' = tongue tip on the ridge.

text: The long road leads to Rome.
pedagogical_cue: 'Road' and 'Rome' = no tap, no trill; 'long' and 'leads' = tip touching behind the teeth.

text: Correct the wrong lines, please.
pedagogical_cue: 'Wrong' starts with a smooth English /r/ — never a trill; 'lines' starts with a clear /l/.

text: I really like your new glasses.
pedagogical_cue: 'Really' has /r/ then /l/: tongue back and free, then tip up to the ridge.

text: Fresh fruit grows in the valley.
pedagogical_cue: Keep the /r/ in 'fresh', 'fruit' and 'grows' soft and untrilled; touch the ridge for 'valley'.

text: Clear rules help everyone learn.
pedagogical_cue: 'Rules' starts with /r/ and ends with /l/ — tongue from back and free to tip-up.

text: The library is closed on Fridays.
pedagogical_cue: 'Library' alternates /l/ and /r/ — tip up for l, tongue back for r, no trills.

text: Turn right at the traffic light.
pedagogical_cue: 'Right' vs 'light': only the tongue tip changes — free for /r/, touching for /l/.

text: Our free plan is really flexible.
pedagogical_cue: In 'free' the /r/ follows /f/ smoothly; in 'plan' and 'flexible' the /l/ follows /p/ and /f/.

text: We planned two projects this quarter.
pedagogical_cue: Release a small puff of air after /p/, /t/ and /k/ at the start of a stressed syllable.

text: Keep track of the sprint plan.
pedagogical_cue: Puff of air on 'keep', 'track' and 'plan'; after /s/ in 'sprint' the /p/ has no puff.

text: Please take a quick break.
pedagogical_cue: Hold a tissue in front of your mouth: it should move on 'please', 'take' and 'quick'.

text: The team completed the task on time.
pedagogical_cue: Aspirate the /t/ in 'team' and 'time' and the /k/ in 'completed' — a short burst of air.

text: Put the cups on the top shelf.
pedagogical_cue: Strong puff on 'put', 'cups' and 'top'; don't let them sound like 'b', 'g' or 'd'.

text: Click the play button twice.
pedagogical_cue: 'Click', 'play' and 'twice' start with aspirated stops — air first, then the vowel.

text: Coffee prices went up today.
pedagogical_cue: Breathy release on /k/ in 'coffee', /p/ in 'prices' and /t/ in 'today'.

text: Pick a topic for the talk.
pedagogical_cue: Three aspirated starts: 'pick', 'topic', 'talk' — feel the air on your hand.

text: Our client expects a clear plan.
pedagogical_cue: In /kl/ and /pl/ the puff makes the /l/ slightly breathy — don't add a vowel between.

text: Split the cake into ten pieces.
pedagogical_cue: 'Cake', 'ten' and 'pieces' get a puff; after /s/ in 'split' the /p/ is unaspirated.

text: The train stops at Park Street.
pedagogical_cue: Aspirate 'train' and 'Park'; 'stops' and 'street' start with /s/, so no puff there.

text: Tell Kate the price is correct.
pedagogical_cue: Puff of air on 'tell', 'Kate', 'price' and 'correct' — no voicing until the vowel.

text: My bed is not that bad.
pedagogical_cue: 'Bad' = jaw drops low, mouth wide; 'bed' = jaw only half open.

text: Set the bag on that desk.
pedagogical_cue: Open wide for 'bag' and 'that'; keep the jaw higher for 'set' and 'desk'.

text: I had a headache yesterday.
pedagogical_cue: 'Had' = wide, low /æ/; 'head' and 'yes' = mid /ɛ/.

text: Pack your pens and maps.
pedagogical_cue: 'Pack' and 'maps' = drop the jaw; 'pens' = smaller mouth, tongue higher.

text: Send the plan to Anna.
pedagogical_cue: 'Plan' and 'Anna' open wide like a yawn; 'send' stays mid-open.

text: My dad left a message.
pedagogical_cue: 'Dad' = low and wide; 'left' and 'message' = mid /ɛ/ — don't make them the same.

text: That pan is better than this pen.
pedagogical_cue: 'Pan' vs 'pen': drop the jaw for the first, lift it for the second.

text: Help me pack this bag.
pedagogical_cue: 'Help' is mid /ɛ/; 'pack' and 'bag' are low, wide /æ/.

text: The cat sat next to Ben.
pedagogical_cue: 'Cat' and 'sat' = jaw low; 'next' and 'Ben' = jaw mid.

text: Every family has a plan.
pedagogical_cue: 'Every' starts with mid /ɛ/; 'family', 'has' and 'plan' open wide with /æ/.

text: Grab a snack before the test.
pedagogical_cue: 'Grab' and 'snack' = wide /æ/; 'test' = mid /ɛ/.

text: He sent the man a letter.
pedagogical_cue: 'Man' = wide /æ/; 'sent' and 'letter' = mid /ɛ/ — 'man' and 'men' must differ.
